notes: The published site coordinates (23.6304 N, 70.8407 E), the Wikipedia and OpenStreetMap points and the publication's own 23 deg 37' N, 70 deg 50' E all fall on scrub and fields about 8 km west of the excavated site, with no structures. The site was found from a web place listing ('Surkotada Indus Valley Civilization', 23.611254 N, 70.917418 E): the imagery there shows an exposed walled complex. It was matched to the plan by viewing the plan reduced to the imagery scale beside the imagery: the room rows against a western rampart, the free-standing house 3 north of them, the gateway complex projecting south and the platform west of Bastion-2 all coincide. Wayback release 8432 (World Imagery Wayback 2021-07-21) holds a WorldView-3 image of 2018-12-18 that shows the walls more sharply than the current Vantor image of 2026-03-26; points were read on release 8432, from gridded crops of the mosaic and of a grey-scale contrast-stretched copy in the same pixel frame (crops/surk_main_w8432_gray_enh_sameframe.png, crops/surk_main_w8432_gray_ac_sameframe.png). The same structures are visible, unchanged, in the 2026 image. Only the citadel's south-west quarter and the gateway are exposed, so all four points lie within about 90 m by 60 m of the plan's 125 m by 100 m extent. No statement of a wall's or the town's orientation was met in the Surkotada publication pages read (List of Figures, Introduction, site description, pp. 14-15).
